note: Mutation cases for tools/mutate.py -- read that file's docstring first. One case per independently falsifiable CHANNEL of the three frozen oracles plus data/combat_vectors.json and data/rng_vectors.json: each perturbs the smallest thing that isolates one claim, and the named test must go red with `expect` in its output. Several mutations that all red the same assertion would be noise, so there is at most one per channel. A channel NOT listed here has not been shown to be falsifiable. Nothing here is ever applied to the real files: the runner works on a copy.
manifest_lives_here_because: This is configuration for a tool, not captured data. data/ is the read-only ground-truth tree the gate exists to protect, and a manifest living there would be copied -- and mutable -- inside the gate's own shadow of it.
findings: Cases carrying "expect_red": false are not coverage. Each is a column the captures hold that no assertion reads -- found by this gate on its first run, by mutating the column and watching the whole test binary stay green. They are kept here, and kept executable, so the record cannot rot: when an assertion finally reaches one, the gate fails on it and the case is promoted to a red one. SCOPE OF THE SILENCE: each of these runs ONE cargo test binary, so what it establishes is that no RUST test in that binary reads the column. That a Python test does not read it either was checked by hand (git grep, fix round 1) and is NOT what the gate watches; a Python-side assertion arriving on one of these columns would not fail the case. Registering a finding whose test is a Python command is allowed -- the manifest and the runner take any argv -- so a future finding on that side can be recorded the same way.

cases.label: frozen-oracle-refusal
cases.defends: tools/rngtrace/combattrace.py refuses `--out` naming a frozen oracle before it writes anything, and tools/test_rngtrace.py's test_the_fold_refuses_to_write_over_a_frozen_oracle proves it. This is the Python arm: the artifact perturbed is the GUARD, not an oracle.

mutate.from:
if named is not None:
            ap.error("--out %s names %s, a FROZEN oracle: it is read for its "
                     "SHA-256 and never written.  Write the fight oracle to "
                     "data/combat_trace.json instead." % (args.out, named))
mutate.to:
if named is not None:
            pass

cases.expect: combattrace.main() accepted --out naming a FROZEN oracle

The appended site is a real instruction at a real boundary, so only the closure comparison can catch it.

cases.label: combat-dispatch-random-sites
cases.defends: the four Random sites the brief asked for are the ONLY ones in [0x4900, 0x5080) -- a byte scan for `9a 4b 11 78 0f`, not a list.  A whole-battle differential replay desynchronises on any draw site this misses.

cases.label: combat-dispatch-unreachable-line
cases.defends: `1000:4e2a is dead code` rests on there being no jump into [1000:4e12, 1000:4e43), so fall-through is the only entry.  Widening the range to 1000:4dde puts a real branch target (1000:4deb, from 1000:4de3) inside it, which is what the scan has to notice -- otherwise `no second entry` is `I did not find one`.

cases.label: combat-dispatch-bill-mantissa-low
cases.defends: the hospital bill's `ratio 0.6 needs no exponent bias` reads each significand off its `di` word ALONE, which is only valid because 1000:4ff8 and 1000:5005 zero the low mantissa half.  Task 17's review found that premise stated with no address and checked by nothing.  The perturbation swaps in a DIFFERENT real instruction at a real boundary -- 1000:4ff5 `mov cx,0x83` -- so the identity check passes and only the `xor si,si` assertion can catch it.
cases.expect: not the `xor si,si` that makes the low mantissa half zero

cases.label: save-layout-growth-log-offset
cases.defends: tests/progression.rs::the_shipped_saves_hold_one_growth_log_entry_per_level_reached reads the growth log out of all five shipped saves at the offset data/save_layout.json names, and requires exactly `level` two-code entries and nothing past them.  Task 18 made that offset load-bearing for the flee penalty: `20ae:38cf + level*3` is Borland's BIASED base for an array[1..40] of string[2] whose real base is `20ae:38d2`, so an off-by-three here reads the neighbouring entry and the de-level takes back the wrong two stats.  A +3 shift makes every entry read its successor's, so SAVE_R0's last real entry (15, its level) comes back empty.  (Task 19 named every byte of the two former `unk_` spans, which moved this field's INDEX in the array from 16 to 39; the offset it carries is unchanged.)

cases.label: save-layout-record-base-delta
cases.defends: Task 19's whole per-byte table rests on one claim: `.SAV` offset + 0x369c IS the DGROUP address of the same byte, because the record is moved by an untyped BlockRead/BlockWrite against `DS:369c` (1000:6c01, 1000:acc3, 1000:7658).  Every `guest` address in data/save_layout.json is checked against that delta.  Shift one `guest` by a single byte -- to the DGROUP address of the NEXT field, which is a real address the image really references -- and only the delta check can catch it.

cases.label: save-layout-evidence-names-the-right-byte
cases.defends: each field's `evidence` is the instruction that reads or writes that byte, and the character sheet's flag lines are what attribute a label to an address.  Swapping two neighbouring sheet guards -- both real, both aligned, both inside FUN_1000_1a03 -- keeps every structural property of the artifact and changes only WHICH byte the label belongs to, which is the mistake docs/re/character-sheet.md says its own table exists to prevent.

cases.label: save-layout-cartridges-is-a-word
cases.defends: `.SAV 0x2b3` (20ae:394f), the cartridge count, is a WORD and not a byte: the character sheet's guard at 1000:1d8a is `cmp word [0x394f],0` and 20ae:3950 has no reference of its own image-wide.  Task 19's brief carried it as a byte (`0x2b3` reading `0,0,0,0,8` across the saves).  Demoting it to a u8 leaves the field tiling intact only if the high half becomes a field too, so the check that catches it is the one that asserts the SIGNED WORD set, not the partition.  Its `expect` was `"Ran"` in the first revision, which appears in every unittest run green or red -- the gate's own rule 4 exists to stop exactly that, so the case was weakened to its red-exit check alone.  It now quotes the census assertion's message, which only this assertion emits.

cases.label: character-sheet-port-literal
cases.defends: tools/test_character_sheet_port.py decodes the Russian string literals src/character_sheet.rs actually SHIPS out of orig/g.exe.  tools/test_string_citations.py checks the BACKTICKED literal in the comment beside a CS citation, never the double-quoted one in the code, so before this scanner a comment could be right while the string the player sees was one character wrong.  The perturbation is a Cyrillic `с` typed as a Latin `c`, which renders identically in a diff.

cases.label: character-sheet-port-citation
cases.defends: tools/test_character_sheet_port.py pins each CS citation in src/character_sheet.rs to the literal beside it, splitting a format! template on its {...} placeholders first.  0x196e and 0x1983 are the two suit labels 21 bytes apart, both real, and both cited CORRECTLY elsewhere in the same file -- the Task 19 defect class, which only decoding the bytes tells apart.
cases.expect: which is not a fragment of

cases.label: character-sheet-port-citation-order
cases.defends: The citations naming ONE format! template are pinned to its fragments IN ORDER, not to the fragment SET.  Until the Task 22 final review this check tested set membership, so the stat line's five citations (0x16b7, 0x16bc, 0x16c5, 0x16ce, 0x16d7) could be permuted among themselves and stay green -- 7 of the file's 59 citations were pinned to the group rather than to the fragment.  The perturbation renames the FIRST citation to the FOURTH's offset, so the group's first decoded fragment is the one that belongs fourth.  Both offsets are real, both still occur in the file, and nothing but the order is wrong -- which is exactly what set membership could not see.

cases.label: shop-arms-instruction-identity
cases.defends: tools/test_shop_arms.py walks every {addr,text} record in data/shop_arms.json and requires orig/g.exe to decode that instruction at that address -- the identity half of the two signals docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md keeps apart.

cases.label: shop-arms-literal-identity
cases.defends: Every {cs_offset,text} record must be the Pascal shortstring actually at that CS offset.  This is what stops a refusal or a confirmation being attributed to the wrong arm -- the six bmar arms push 22 literal records over 21 distinct literals, and rows 2 and 4 genuinely share one (CS 0x93b0).

cases.label: shop-arms-strings-completeness
cases.defends: strings[] is the WHOLE set of CS literals an arm pushes, measured by decoding the arm's span and collecting every `mov di,imm` followed by `push cs`/`push di`.  So "this arm prints nothing else" -- the claim the port's confirmation and refusal wording rests on -- is a measurement over the span, not a list that stopped being written.

cases.label: shop-arms-district-negative
cases.defends: The "no arm of bmar rows 1..6 tests the district" claim is a NEGATIVE, and it rests on one aligned decode covering the whole 1000:c8ce..1000:ccc4 span.  The recorded instruction count is what proves the walk covered it rather than stopping early -- without it an empty hit list could mean an empty search.

cases.label: shop-arms-club-bug-counterexample
cases.defends: The club-without-knuckles bug is the DIFFERENCE between the shop arm at 1000:cc69 and the combat loot arm at 1000:55d8, which tests the same flag for the same item and HAS the without-knuckles branch.  So the loot arm's `add word [0x38a8],0x4` is re-derived too; without it the bug claim would be one site quoted against itself.

cases.label: shop-arms-district-inventory-complete
cases.defends: district_gates_are_menu_only is asserted SET-EQUAL to every `cmp byte [0x3692],imm` site in 1000:c4be..1000:ccd8, so a MISSING entry reds -- not merely a wrong one.  Fix round 1 found this artifact listing two of the five gates while every listed entry decoded correctly and every check passed: the recurring defect is an inventory whose completeness claim stopped the next search.  The perturbation points the row-9 entry at the row-8 gate, which decodes to the very same instruction, so nothing but the COUNT of distinct gates changes -- five sites, four recorded.

cases.label: shop-arms-gates-completeness
cases.defends: gates[] is measured against every conditional branch in the arm's span, the analogue of the strings[] sweep.  A SILENT omitted gate prints nothing, so the strings sweep cannot see it, and `no gate in rows 1..6 refuses silently` is a headline claim.  The perturbation renames row 5's already-own branch so the arm's six conditional branches are accounted for by five.

cases.label: shop-arms-club-bug-adds-pinned-by-address
cases.defends: bugs[].where.adds is pinned by ADDRESS inside row 6's span, not by decoded text.  The loot arm's 1000:55da / 1000:55df spell the same two instructions, so a text-only comparison passed with the bug record citing the counter-example's own adds -- which would have made the finding one site quoted against itself.  The perturbation swaps in exactly those two addresses.

cases.label: mar-arms-district-inventory-complete
cases.defends: `mar` is the shop where the district DOES reach the buy path, so its gate inventory is a POSITIVE claim and can carry the same defect a negative one can -- an inventory whose completeness claim stopped the next search.  buy_path_gates + menu_gates is asserted SET-EQUAL to every [0x3692] operand an aligned decode of 1000:b94a..1000:c31f finds, and to a raw `92 36` byte scan over the same range.  The perturbation points the row-9 menu gate at the row-8 one, which is still a real gate site at a real boundary, so only the COUNT of distinct recorded gates changes: six sites, five recorded.

cases.label: mar-arms-row-7-gap-is-measured-not-asserted
cases.defends: The row-7 finding is the DIFFERENCE between the rows the menu hides and the rows the buy path gates, and a difference is worth nothing if either set is a list that stopped being written.  Which menu lines a menu gate covers is MEASURED -- the price-byte operands an aligned decode of the gate's own listed range finds -- and cross-checked against data/shops.json.  The perturbation drops row 7 from the first menu gate's coverage, which is exactly the shape of a hand-written list that stopped one entry early.

cases.label: mar-arms-gates-completeness
cases.defends: The gates[] sweep counts every conditional branch in a mar row's span, including the SILENT district gate in front of rows 6, 8 and 9 -- the one test in either handler that prints nothing, so the strings sweep cannot see it.  The perturbation renames row 6's district branch to its afford branch, leaving five branches in the span accounted for by four.

cases.label: mar-arms-strings-completeness
cases.defends: strings[] is the WHOLE set of CS literals a mar arm pushes, measured over the arm's span.  Five mar literals are shared between two rows (0x8ef9, 0x8f6d, 0x8f94, 0x8fc8, 0x8ff3), so attributing a refusal to the wrong arm is exactly the error to guard against here.  The perturbation moves row 7's afford refusal one byte on, where nothing pushes it.

cases.label: mar-arms-upgrade-split-is-exclusive
cases.defends: Rows 7, 8 and 9 add the upgrade DELTA when the lesser item is owned and the full bonus when it is not, and the two arms are exclusive only because the delta arm jumps over the full one; a port applying both would over-grant.  The three rejoins are also the instructions docs/re/shop-arms.md shows inside a fence, where the prose checker cannot reach them.  The perturbation swaps row 8's rejoin RECORD for row 7's, address and text together, so the identity walk still passes and only the geometry is wrong -- the substituted jump sits outside row 8's split.
cases.expect: does not sit between the delta arm

cases.label: mar-arms-effects-completeness
cases.defends: effects[] is the WHOLE set of absolute memory writes in an arm's span, swept and asserted set-equal -- not just a list whose entries decode.  Two mar claims are statements about that whole set: row 2's Random(3) `changes no state at all`, and `no global a mar arm writes is write-only`.  Fix round 1 promoted this because the inventory was factually complete and held by nothing.  The perturbation points row 4's armour write at row 7's, which decodes to the SAME instruction (`inc [0x38b2]`) at a real boundary, so the identity walk still passes and only the span membership is wrong.

cases.label: mar-arms-random-site-completeness
cases.defends: Every `Random` draw an arm makes advances the RNG stream whether or not its result is used -- mar row 2's is purely cosmetic and still moves it -- so `docs/re/shop-arms.md`'s Task-26 directive rests on the recorded draws being ALL of them.  The guard sweeps the five-byte `9a 4b 11 78 0f` far-call signature over each span instead of confirming the recorded ones decode.  The perturbation points row 2's call at bmar row 3's, which is the same five bytes at a real boundary but outside the span.

cases.label: mar-arms-district-sweep-start-is-anchored
cases.defends: A completeness sweep is only as good as its RANGE.  Both district tests used to assert nothing stronger than `sweep_start < first_arm`, and fix round 1 narrowed mar's start from 1000:b94a to 1000:bb80 -- skipping two of the six gates -- with both tests still green.  The start is now pinned to the handler's own verb compare, which the artifact already carried as `shop_tag_at` and nothing asserted.  The perturbation is exactly that narrowing, to a real instruction boundary that is still before the arms.

cases.label: den-arms-instruction-identity
cases.defends: tools/test_den_arms.py walks every {addr,text} record in data/den_arms.json and requires orig/g.exe to decode that instruction at that address -- the identity half of the two signals docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md keeps apart.

cases.label: den-arms-literal-identity

cases.label: den-arms-strings-completeness
cases.defends: strings[] is the WHOLE set of CS literals the handler pushes, measured by decoding 1000:d802..1000:df06 and collecting every `mov di,imm` followed by `push cs`/`push di`.  So `the w arm prints nothing` and `this arm prints nothing else` are measurements over the range, not lists that stopped being written.

cases.label: den-arms-gates-completeness
cases.defends: Every CONDITIONAL branch in 1000:d802..1000:df06 must be named somewhere in data/den_arms.json, cross-checked against data/branches.json's independent Ghidra-generated population.  The string sweep cannot see a SILENT gate, and `an unrecognised key is silent` and `the d arm's two gates print nothing` are headline claims of docs/re/den.md.

cases.label: den-arms-random-site-completeness
cases.defends: A draw nobody recorded still advances the RNG stream and would desynchronise every trace after it, so draws[] is set-equal to a sweep of the five-byte `call 0f78:114b` signature over the whole range -- cross-checked against a raw byte count so an aligned miss and a byte-scan miss cannot cancel out.

cases.label: den-arms-draw-n-is-rederived
cases.defends: Each draw's `n` is re-derived with tools/re_query.py's own walk-back over the pushing idiom, never copied from the artifact.  district*15 and district*10 differ by one immediate byte and the `d` arm uses both.

cases.label: den-arms-effects-completeness
cases.defends: effects[] is set-equal to every instruction in the range that WRITES an absolute-memory operand, with the read and write buckets asserted EXHAUSTIVE so an unclassified shape fails instead of vanishing.  This is what makes `the s arm writes nothing` a measurement.
cases.expect: is not the set of absolute writes in

cases.label: den-arms-silent-arm-is-measured
cases.defends: `s` and `w` claim to write nothing.  The claim is checked by sweeping their own spans for absolute writes, so a span narrowed to dodge a store fails rather than passing quietly.

cases.label: den-arms-threshold-blocks-differ
cases.defends: The headline finding: 1000:d90f and 1000:da6e are byte-identical and 1000:dcba is a DIFFERENT predicate, nine bytes shorter.  Folding all three into one helper during the porting task is the exact mistake this case exists to catch, so the bytes are re-sliced out of orig/g.exe rather than compared with the artifact's own copy.
cases.expect: the artifact's byte string is not what is at

cases.label: den-arms-threshold-multiplier
cases.defends: Each block's recorded FORMULA is read back off its own arithmetic -- two `shl ax,1` plus an `add ax,si` is *5, one `shl ax,1` alone is *2 -- so a formula that says the wrong multiplier fails even when every address in it is right.

cases.label: den-arms-fight-param-inventory
cases.defends: `param_1 == 5 has no compare of its own in FUN_1000_3d11` is a NEGATIVE over another function, and it is the whole reason Task 28 cannot port the two den fights.  The eight [bp+0x4] sites are set-equal to an aligned sweep, and the sweep's own instruction count is asserted so an empty hit list cannot mean an empty search.

cases.label: den-arms-fight-param-dispatch-chain
cases.defends: The `[bp+0x4]` sweep alone is NOT enough: 1000:3d24 copies the parameter into `al` and the real dispatch is a chain of REGISTER compares no such scan can see.  A first draft of fight_param_finding had only that sweep.  So the `cmp al,imm8` population is swept too, set-equal to the recorded chain, and the chain's contiguity is asserted -- nothing runs between one link's miss and the next link's compare, which is what makes a register compare readable as a parameter test.

cases.label: den-arms-fight-param-chain-contiguity
cases.defends: The chain link that matters most is 1000:3d2b -> 1000:3e8d, which is bridged by the single `jmp` at 1000:3d2f.  If anything else ran there, `al` would no longer hold the parameter and the whole register-compare reading would collapse.  The bridge is decoded, not assumed.

cases.label: den-arms-call-target-wraps
cases.defends: All five near calls out of the den encode a rel16 that WRAPS: 1000:dc0e sums to image 0x10d14 and reaches 1000:0d14.  A check that compared the un-wrapped sum would find none of them, which is the mistake tools/re_derive.py's near_calls_to already documents.

cases.label: den-arms-range-instruction-count
cases.defends: Every sweep in this file rests on the aligned decode covering the whole range.  The instruction count is the anchor that proves it did, so a walk that stopped early cannot pass as a search that found nothing.

cases.label: den-arms-boundary-exemption-is-honest
cases.defends: known_not_boundaries lets the artifact NAME an address it does not claim is a boundary -- the wrong 1000:2536 in docs/re/save-format.md.  Each entry is asserted to really NOT be a boundary, so the exemption cannot be used to park a good address and skip the check on it.
cases.expect: the exemption is hiding a good address

cases.label: den-arms-globals-write-lists
cases.defends: globals[] carries, per DGROUP address, exactly the writes to it inside the range -- re-derived by sweeping the decode, not by trusting the list.  20ae:38cb is written twice and 20ae:3b7a four times, so a dropped entry is easy and invisible otherwise.

cases.label: den-arms-ds-push-completeness
cases.defends: 20ae:3a72 is the den's own buffer and 20ae:3972 is the street's; the `pr` and `kl` verbs are compared against the STREET one and all seven den keys against the den's.  The pointer-push inventory is set-equal to a sweep so that distinction cannot rot.

cases.label: den-arms-spans-tile
cases.defends: The seven arm spans must chain end-to-start and reach from the case-fold call to the discovery refusal, so a block cannot be dropped out of the map by being left out of every span -- which is how the effects and strings sweeps could be narrowed without any of them going red.

cases.label: den-arms-loop-back-edge
cases.defends: `the menu prints once and only the prompt repeats` rests on 1000:dede targeting 1000:dae2, the prompt push, and on that push carrying the prompt literal.  Both halves are re-derived from the branch displacement and the operand.
cases.expect: not to the recorded loop top

cases.label: den-arms-key-set-from-compares
cases.defends: Each of the seven keys is established at a `call 0f78:0bd8` on the den's own buffer, and the CS literal at the recorded offset must BE that key -- `hp` in particular, which src/commands.rs had only from a menu string.

cases.label: den-arms-prose-fence-identity
cases.defends: docs/re/den.md pastes a hundred-odd disassembly lines inside fences; each is re-decoded from orig/g.exe.  The prose and data/den_arms.json are the two places the same claims live, and a fence is where a hand-edited instruction would hide.

cases.label: den-arms-prose-embedded-instruction-identity
cases.defends: The identity hole fix round 1 closed.  `test_every_cited_instruction_decodes_to_what_the_artifact_says` only walks dicts with SEPARATE `addr` and `text` keys, so an instruction claim written inside a prose sentence -- `1000:4a49` with the text `dec [0x38a4]`, which shipped -- escaped it, escaped the boundary walk (the address IS aligned, it is just a different instruction), and escaped the markdown scans because it lives only in the JSON.  Every such span in every string value is now decoded.  The perturbation below is the exact shape that shipped wrong.

mutate.from: `1000:dc79 push [0x38cb]` is a READ -- the `#` substitution for the first line. The threshold arithmetic at `1000:dc8e`..`1000:dc9b` does NOT `dec ax` first, unlike all three threshold blocks: it is `district*10 + 10`, not `(district-1)*10`.
mutate.to: `1000:dc79 dec [0x38cb]` is a READ -- the `#` substitution for the first line. The threshold arithmetic at `1000:dc8e`..`1000:dc9b` does NOT `dec ax` first, unlike all three threshold blocks: it is `district*10 + 10`, not `(district-1)*10`.

cases.expect: inside a prose string, but orig/g.exe decodes

cases.label: den-arms-globals-writer-census
cases.defends: Brief item 2 says to name each global from its writers and readers with `tools/re_query.py xrefs-to`, never from the adjacent string.  Nothing re-derived that until fix round 1, and the shipped file claimed `1000:ab92` was 20ae:3692's ONLY writer when `xrefs-to` returns three more.  The image-wide writer set is now re-derived per global, so a completeness claim that stopped the next search goes red.

cases.label: den-arms-globals-xref-counts
cases.defends: The raw / accepted / discarded census beside each global must be what `re_query.xrefs_to` actually reports.  20ae:3b72 is the one global with discards (3 of 12 raw hits are byte-scan straddles), and `of its nine accepted references exactly one is a load` rests on that number being right.

cases.label: sell-spans-tile-the-range
cases.defends: Every other sell sweep is measured over the whole range, so a per-arm span that overlapped or skipped its neighbour would leave the per-span records describing bytes no sweep saw.  The eleven spans are asserted to tile 1000:ce76..1000:d383 exactly and to sum to sweeps.instructions.

cases.label: sell-range-end-is-measured
cases.defends: Task 28 shipped a residue whose interval ran 282 bytes past the arm's real end because the bound came from a brief.  The sell range's right-hand end is instead established by decoding all 7742 instructions of `entry` and finding the one near branch that targets 1000:d383.
cases.expect: does not end where the range does

cases.label: sell-range-entry-edges-complete
cases.defends: `range.entered_from` claims to be every edge into 1000:ce76.  Appending a real branch that goes somewhere else must red, or the list would be a set of addresses nobody compared against the branch graph.

value.what: not an entry edge at all

cases.label: sell-gates-completeness
cases.defends: All twelve gates in the sell range are SILENT -- they print nothing -- so the strings sweep cannot catch one that was left out.  Every conditional branch in the range must be named by the artifact; pointing two conjuncts at the same address drops one.
cases.expect: an unrecorded branch is an unrecorded gate

cases.label: sell-strings-completeness
cases.defends: `this arm prints nothing else` is what the port's offer and confirmation wording rests on.  It is a measurement over the range: every `mov di,imm` followed by `push cs`/`push di` must be a recorded literal, and vice versa.

cases.label: sell-effects-completeness
cases.defends: `nothing is unwound on a sale` is a claim about the WHOLE set of writes in the range, not about the three each arm lists.  The WRITE bucket is asserted set-equal to effects[] plus the prologue.

cases.label: sell-random-site-completeness
cases.defends: One `wes` can spend six draws.  A draw nobody recorded still advances the RNG stream, so the six sites come from a sweep of the five-byte `Random` signature rather than from the artifact.

cases.label: sell-refund-n-is-rederived
cases.defends: The refund finding is the whole point of this map.  Each arm's `n` is recovered by `re_query.pushed_n` walking back from the call site, not read out of the artifact -- otherwise the refund table would be a copy of itself.

cases.label: sell-refund-base-is-rederived
cases.defends: The other half of the same constant: the base comes from decoding the `add ax,imm` that follows the draw.

cases.label: sell-dgroup-set-is-complete
cases.defends: `the refund reads no price byte` and `nothing is unwound` are both negatives over the complete set of DGROUP addresses the range references.  That set is asserted equal to the decode, so the two assertNotIns are statements about everything rather than about a list someone stopped writing.
cases.expect: the DGROUP addresses the range references are

cases.label: sell-ladder-requires-matches-the-conjuncts
cases.defends: `own plus a better rung` is the finding the brief called a hypothesis.  The prose-level `requires_any_of` and the decoded conjunct chain must name the same flags, or the ladder could be described one way and tested another.

cases.label: sell-arms-are-sequential
cases.defends: `one wes can sell up to six items` rests on there being NO jump between an arm's confirmation and the next arm's own-flag test.  Pointing the confirmation at another arm's WriteLn must red.
cases.expect: so the arms are not sequential

cases.label: sell-roll-precedes-the-answer
cases.defends: Two findings rest on ORDER alone: the draw is spent even when the offer is declined, and the `nothing to sell` line means `nothing was OFFERED`.  Both are the position of `mov [0x3e33],al` relative to the yes/no compare, which every other check here is blind to.
cases.expect: stores its roll AFTER the yes/no compare

cases.label: sell-junk-credit-has-no-rate
cases.defends: `x` credits the junk one-for-one.  The claim is the ABSENCE of anything between the load and the add, so the six-instruction path is recorded verbatim and compared against the decode.
cases.expect: the one-for-one claim is exactly the absence

cases.label: sell-globals-xref-counts
cases.defends: The raw / accepted / discarded census beside each sell global must be what `re_query.xrefs_to` reports.  20ae:38ba is the one with a discard (a byte-scan hit inside `mov dx,0x138`), and dropping it would make the operand-field filter look like it never fires.

cases.label: sell-globals-writer-census
cases.defends: `there is no equipped bit` rests on each item flag's complete image-wide writer set being a purchase arm, a loot arm or a sell arm.  The sets are recomputed from the scan, not trusted.
cases.expect: the image-wide writer set is not what the artifact

cases.label: sell-scratch-byte-is-private
cases.defends: 20ae:3e33 has no name to borrow: it is named from its own use, and that is only honest because all twenty of its image-wide references are inside this range.
cases.expect: is not the private scratch byte

cases.label: sell-arithmetic-coincidence-is-recomputed
cases.defends: The one numeric relation this map states is a COINCIDENCE between two sets of literals, and the danger is a later reader turning it into a formula.  Both halves are recomputed from the recorded prices and constants.
cases.expect: no longer holds for every priced arm

cases.label: sell-tail-loops-back-to-the-prompt
cases.defends: Both sub-verbs return to 1000:c88e, the prompt push, and NOT to the menu -- so the dealers do not reprint nine lines after a sale.  The target is decoded from the jump rather than asserted.

cases.label: sell-item-flag-names-from-the-sheet
cases.defends: Task 27's review turned on three `named_from` values that were never re-derived.  Each of the ten item flags is named from the character sheet's own line, and both halves -- the guard that tests the flag and the push of the label -- are decoded here.

cases.label: sell-sweeps-range-is-the-block's-range
cases.defends: Every count under `sell.sweeps` is a measurement over one interval.  If `sweeps.range` could drift from the range the arms tile, the counts would still be internally consistent and would be describing different bytes.

cases.label: sell-ds-pointer-push-count
cases.defends: The strings sweep keeps only `mov di,imm` followed by `push cs`/`push di` and must ignore the 28 buffer pushes that use `push ds`.  Counting the ignored population is what stops the filter silently swallowing a CS push it should have measured.

cases.label: sell-ladders-are-a-view-of-the-arms
cases.defends: `ladder_finding.ladders[]` is the finding stated in item terms; it has to be derivable from the six arms rather than written beside them, or the prose could describe one ladder while the binary tests another.
cases.expect: `sellable` is not the rungs an arm actually clears

cases.label: shop-arms-artifact-free-text-addresses-are-boundaries
cases.defends: The hole Task 29's review found.  `insn_records` and `literal_records` walk dicts with SEPARATE keys, so a `1000:xxxx` written inside a `note`, `what`, `claim` or `named_from` sentence reached `at()` through nothing -- while the same address in docs/re/shop-arms.md IS swept by ProseTest.  Task 29 shipped `1000:ce8e`..`1000:ce99` into sell.what_the_port_must_change[0] through exactly that gap: 1000:ce99 is the last BYTE of 1000:ce97 and decodes as `cmp [bx-0x6930],bh`.  Every string value in the whole artifact is now scanned.
cases.expect: in free text, and an aligned decode

cases.label: shop-arms-prose-embedded-instruction-identity
cases.defends: The identity half of the same hole.  An address written inside a sentence WITH its mnemonic passes the boundary sweep -- it is aligned, it is just a different instruction -- and nothing compared the mnemonic against orig/g.exe.  Task 27 found three false provenance claims in data/den_arms.json through this exact shape; this is its twin for data/shop_arms.json.

mutate.from: The miss is the inverted pair `1000:cedd jz 0xcee2` over `1000:cedf jmp 0xd36d` -- it skips the whole sell block and lands on the handler's shared exit compare with the typed line intact.
mutate.to: The miss is the inverted pair `1000:cedd jz 0xcee3` over `1000:cedf jmp 0xd36d` -- it skips the whole sell block and lands on the handler's shared exit compare with the typed line intact.

cases.expect: inside a prose string, but orig/g.exe decodes

cases.label: shop-arms-selltest-count-is-guarded
cases.defends: Task 29 advertised `SellTest` as sixteen cases, twice, against a class of seventeen -- a count in the shipped map that nothing checked.  The doc's two mentions are now compared against unittest.TestLoader's own case list, so the count cannot drift from the class in either direction.

cases.label: trim-inventory-counts-are-checked
cases.defends: docs/re/gaps.md's trimmed-prompt inventory went stale FOUR times -- three as a pasted grep listing whose line numbers shifted, and once more after it became a command, when Task 30 added `Game::sell_offer` as the tenth call site and updated nothing.  Making the numbers recomputable did not make anything recompute them, which is the `inventory whose completeness claim stopped the next search` defect docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md names.  TrimInventoryTest reruns the entry's own filter over src/*.rs and compares BOTH the counts in its sentence and the `where` column of its table.  This case perturbs the DOCUMENT side; the src side was checked by hand the same way -- one extra `.trim()` in src/text.rs reddens both of the test's assertions.

mutate.from: **Sixteen hits: ten call sites and six lines of prose about them.**
mutate.to: **Fifteen hits: nine call sites and six lines of prose about them.**

cases.expect: says 9 call sites and 6 prose lines

cases.label: sell-arm-immediates-come-from-the-artifact
cases.defends: The whole-branch review's I1.  src/game.rs's each_wes_arm_sells_its_own_item_for_its_own_two_immediates used to follow `delta == base + r` with `(base..base+span).contains(&delta)` and a doc comment claiming neither check subsumed the other.  It did: Rng::below_at computes `((r * n) >> 32) as u16`, which is `< n` by construction, so given `log[0].n == span` the range assertion could not fail -- the tautological comparison presented as verification that docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md names.  The replacement compares the test table's site, base and span against data/shop_arms.json's sell.arms[].roll, which tools/test_shop_arms.py re-derives from orig/g.exe, so the arm's payout is chained to the binary's own immediates.  Moving arm 1's `add ax,0x8` base off 8 must redden it.

cases.label: all-six-sell-credits-come-from-the-artifact
cases.defends: The second instance of I1, in one_wes_sells_all_six_items_and_never_the_cleaver: an exact `assert_eq!(money, expect)` was followed by `(105..=163).contains(&money)`, which cannot fail once `expect` is the sum of the same six bases and every drawn `r < n`.  The envelope is gone and the six sites and six bases now come from data/shop_arms.json's sell.arms[].roll rather than from literals restating the table above them.  Moving arm 3's `add ax,0xd` base off 13 must redden the exact sum.

cases.label: out-of-record-inventory-is-guarded
cases.defends: The whole-branch review's I2.  src/persist.rs's `What is deliberately NOT here` table claims to enumerate every global this port carries that sits OUTSIDE the 20ae:369c..20ae:3951 record, and it went stale: Task 28 added Game::fight_accepted_3b72 (20ae:3b72, above 0x3951) and no row.  The only guard, every_in_record_address_named_in_game_rs_is_persisted, filters to (lo..hi) and structurally cannot see that half -- the `inventory whose completeness claim stopped the next search` defect docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md names.  every_game_field_is_either_persisted_or_named_out_of_record walks struct Game's own field list and requires each field whose doc names a 20ae: address to be persisted by to_save OR named in the table.  Renaming the row's field must redden it -- which also proves the table slice reads the markdown rows and not this test's own prose mention of the same field.
cases.expect: neither persists it nor lists it in the out-of-record table
